why.title: Why learn agentic engineering
why.tagline: AI scales the breadth. You set the depth.
paragraphs: The work is shifting. The scarce skill is no longer typing code as fast as possible, but directing agents and verifying their work. Whoever learns that suddenly covers far more ground: many files at once, the repetitive passes, the dull groundwork, and the tests you otherwise keep putting off. The time you win back goes to the questions that truly matter, and to the depth only a human can deliver.

To do this well, it helps to follow training so you can judge where and how to deploy an agent, and which tools you are better off giving it or not. An agent sounds just as confident when it is wrong as when it is right. "Done" is not the same as "proven". When you give an agent free rein over your system, the consequences can have real impact. The difference between an agent that moves you forward and one that does damage is not luck but a matter of craftsmanship: it shows in scoping the agent well and always verifying. That craftsmanship is what you learn in these trainings.

Agents give you a structured way of working for exactly that, a handhold in the sprawl of new AI concepts. You do not need to memorize every term. You learn an approach that holds while the tools keep changing.
why.qe: For quality engineers this is a natural step. Verification is your craft. In a world full of agents, you become the layer that makes their work reliably deployable. Your role does not disappear, it becomes the linchpin.
